name: Inverted Row on Rings with False Grip
description: The inverted row on rings with a false grip (wrist draped over the rings) is a horizontal pulling exercise that simultaneously trains rowing strength and the grip position required for ring muscle-ups. The unstable ring surface recruits additional stabilizer muscle activity compared to fixed-bar rows, while the false grip develops wrist and forearm strength essential for advanced ring skills.

execution.starting_position: Set rings at approximately waist-to-chest height. Take a false grip on each ring (wrist over the ring, not just fingers gripping the strap). Lean back so the body is at a 30-45 degree angle to the floor, arms extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust ring height to control difficulty — lower = harder. The false grip feels uncomfortable initially; build wrist tolerance gradually.
steps: Step 1: Establish the false grip and lean back into the starting position with arms extended.
Step 2: Keeping the body in a rigid plank, row the chest toward the rings by driving elbows back.
Step 3: At the top, the hands should be at or near the chest with elbows behind the torso.
Step 4: Lower slowly under control back to the extended arm position.
Step 5: Maintain the false grip throughout the entire set.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row up. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Releasing the false grip mid-set — the wrist should remain over the ring
Hips sagging — maintain a rigid plank body line
Pulling with the arms only — initiate with scapular retraction
safety_considerations: The false grip can cause wrist discomfort — build duration gradually
Avoid if you have wrist injuries or tendinopathies
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to hands at chest level.
coaching_cues: Maintain the false grip — wrist over the ring at all times
Lead with the chest, not the chin
Body stays rigid like a plank — no hip hinge
